Bio: Chris Mattmann is the inaugural Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence Officer (CDAIO) at UCLA, a first of its kind position in the UC system. He recently finished a nearly 24 year career at JPL where he conceived, realized and delivered the architecture for the next generation of reusable science data processing systems for NASA's Orbiting Carbon Observatory, NPP Sounder PEATE, and the Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) Earth science missions. Mattmann's work has been funded by NASA, DARPA, DHS, NSF, NIH, NLM and by private industry and commercial partnerships. He contributes to open source and was a member of the Board of Directors at the Apache Software Foundation (2013-18) and was one of the initial contributors to Apache Nutch as a member of its project management committee, the predecessor to Apache Hadoop. Mattmann is the progenitor of the Apache Tika framework, the digital "babel fish" and widely used content analysis and data analytics framework. Mattmann contributes to TensorFlow, Google’s machine learning platform and has recently finished a book on Machine Learning for TensorFlow, 2nd edition published by Manning Publications. Mattmann is an expert in Artificial Intelligence. Mattmann is the Director of the Information Retrieval & Data Science (IRDS) group at USC and Adjunct Research Professor ("Full Professor"). He taught and has incepted graduate courses in Data Science, Web Search Engines & Information Retrieval. Mattmann has materially contributed to understanding of the Deep Web and Dark Web through the DARPA MEMEX project. Mattmann's work helped uncover the Panama Papers scandal which won the Pulitzer Prize in Journalism in 2017. Contact: http://mattmann.ai Represented by Chartwell Speakers.

She is an Apple Distinguished Educator, Apple Teacher, Google for Education Certified Trainer, Adobe Certified Educator, and Microsoft Innovative Educator Expert and Trainer. Maximizing the application and use of AI and ChatGPT, navigating the benefits and concerns for these technologies (including copyright and ethics), building digital citizenship and digital literacy skills, and assuring our students are prepared for today’s world and their futures are all important topics that are relevant in her work with generative AI. Julene serves as an adjunct professor in Lamar University’s Digital Learning and Leading program, a co-instructor with Arizona State University’s Mary Lou Fulton Teacher’s College, and an adjunct professor at Abilene Christian University, Dallas. She is an advisory board member of both Kognity education and Actionable Innovations Global. Julene implemented Learning Studios in Australia, New Zealand, and Azraq Refugee Camp in Jordan with Digital Promise Global and HP as well as UNHDR, CARE, and InZone. Julene coordinated a mobile technology education initiative with iPads in Malawi in collaboration with Lamar Univ., the Univ. of Malawi, UNICEF, and VSO, where she did her doctoral research. She has also worked with Suumu Secondary School in Tanzania. Julene previously directed a series of presentations with INEE, and UNHDR at UNESCO’s Mobile Learning Week in Paris, France. Julene has also worked with Digital Promise, Apple Education, Microsoft Education, Google Education, and Verizon Innovative Learning. Name: Jonny Paterson
Headline: VP, Business and Creative Development at Wall of Entertainment
Bio: Jonny Paterson is an LA-based producer and entertainment executive, and the VP, Business and Creative Development for youth-led digital studio Wall of Entertainment. He is also the founder of JP International Productions and formerly the Head of Development and Vice President of Television at Confluential Films. Earlier in his career he held positions at ICM and Lionsgate before spending 18 months in the office of Paula Wagner ("Mission: Impossible" franchise) at Chestnut Ridge Productions. In 2014 Jonny started JP International Productions and in 2016 he completed his debut feature "Halfway", starring Quinton Aaron ("The Blindside") and Jeffrey DeMunn ("The Shawshank Redemption", "The Green Mile", "The Walking Dead"). "Halfway" received its world premiere in competition at the AFI Dallas International Film Festival in 2016 and was nominated for the Discovery Award at the British Independent Film Awards in 2017. In January 2019, Jonny joined Tommy Oliver's Confluential Films as Head of Development where he built and oversaw their slate of features, scripted and unscripted TV, and premium documentaries with partners that included Sony, Netflix, HBO Docs, Hulu and Peacock among others. Jonny also held the position of Vice President of Television before transitioning to a first-look producing deal with the company in September 2022. Jonny joined Wall of Entertainment in 2025 to head up the company's first international office in Los Angeles. Wall of Entertainment is the youth-led digital content studio behind YouTube original series "Does The Shoe Fit", "The Pink Courtroom", "Minor Issues" and "Shiro's Story" among many others. He is the Executive Producer of Tubi Originals 'Substitute Teacher' and 'House Rules' starring Charles Brockman III and Laro Benz respectively. Both series are slated for release in Summer 2026. Jonny is a recipient of the BAFTA Los Angeles Newcomer Award, was an invited participant at the 2017 Berlinale Talent Campus and sat on the Paley Center's Media Council throughout 2018. A native of Scotland, Jonny received his bachelor's degree in English literature and history from the University of Leeds and his master's degree in entertainment industry management from Carnegie Mellon University. From 2010-2021 Jonny served as a non-Executive director on the board of UK-based charity Football Aid, raising money for good causes with a particular focus on Type-1 diabetes research.

Headline: Co-Owner & CEO, Trilith — The only place on earth where creators don't just make stories. They live inside one.
Bio: Garret Rutherford is the Co-Owner & CEO of Trilith — a first-of-its-kind creative community built around a single purpose: to set the stage and enrich the lives of storymakers who inspire the world. Trilith Studios is the largest purpose-built movie studio in North America — 700 acres, over 1.5 million square feet of production facilities, 32 premium soundstages, construction workshops, costume shops, a 400-acre backlot, and some of the world's most advanced virtual production technology. Current productions include James Gunn's Superman. Creators from MrBeast to the biggest names in Hollywood have made it home. That virtual production capability deserves its own mention: an 18,000 sqft purpose-built stage with a fully enclosed 80' x 90' x 30' LED volume, a flexible ceiling system, and a first-of-its-kind design that lets creatives punch out portions of the screen for lights, cameras, or stunt rigging; infrastructure that used to be out of reach for anyone outside the biggest studios. But Trilith is more than a studio. It's a living, breathing town with 350+ homes, a live event center, a school, and an institute dedicated to the craft of storytelling, all built so storymakers can truly flourish, not just work. Garret is passionate about making sure content creators of every kind know: Trilith was built for you. Whether you're building the next great franchise or your next YouTube series, there's a stage here with your name on it. Consider making Trilith your home!
